1.note: Uzziah's counsel with the prophet is 2 Chronicles 26:5; the print reads כ"ג (23:5). Kept as printed.

2.note: Word printed לפון, not a usual expression; read as 'there is no doubt' (perhaps for לפקפק or ספק).

3.note: The quoted verses are Amos 8:5–6; the print has 5:5, 6. Kept as printed.

4.note: The phrase 'strike hands with the children of strangers' is Isaiah 2:6, not chapter 3. Kept as printed.

5.note: The verse on the seven-day feast is 2 Chronicles 30:21; kept as printed.

6.note: Terse argument; read: a make-up is possible only for a festival kept in its time, so the seven days cannot be explained as a make-up.

7.note: Rare verb (cf. Isaiah 59:19); read as 'stirs, waves'.

8.note: The words 'We have not sinned' are Jeremiah 2:35; kept as printed.

9.note: The verse paraphrased is Jeremiah 7:22; kept as printed.

10.note: Print reads 18:22; the verse is Jeremiah 17:22.

11.note: The Shunammite story is 2 Kings 4:23; kept as printed.

12.note: First letter unclear in the print (ג or נ); read גיסי, 'my brother-in-law'.

13.note: The words are Isaiah 2:6, not chapter 3; kept as printed.

14.note: Print unclear (looks like מ"ז or נ"ז); the tribute is 2 Kings 16:7–8.

15.note: Name blurred in print; probably Drechsler, the commentator on Isaiah.

16.note: Antecedent of הם unclear; read as the precepts coming from the prophet's own will.

17.note: The ruling on gashing by hand or instrument is Makkot 21a; kept as printed.
